data.narrative:
Deep Isolation, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Elizabeth Muller and Richard A. Muller, has raised $26M to date. The nuclear energy sector includes 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and General Matter.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method. Using the $26M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression to the next funding round yields an implied valuation of $52M. This method reflects the expected value expansion between Series A and subsequent stages.

Peer-median comparison is not applicable due to insufficient narrow peer data. While 4 same-sector peers exist, the combination of same-stage and adjacent-stage filtering yielded fewer than 3 comparable datapoints, making a median unreliable. A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable heterogeneity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $44M to $60M, with a median point of $52M. This range reflects stage-typical progression mechanics rather than comprehensive market triangulation. Key uncertainties include the absence of credible same-stage peer multiples and the early-stage nature of the sector, which limits forward visibility on cash burn and capital efficiency relative to peers. Additional funding rounds or market comparables would materially improve valuation precision.
